title: Barrier-Crossing Probabilities for Paired Assignment Signs in Cumulative Experimental Contrasts
banked_reason: D-0.5 NO-PASS: exact paired-even-barrier kernel and calibration consequences are repository-subsumed; two non-identical proposal roots exhausted. Independent main audit confirms no bounded faithful repair; no mathematical refutation or soundness defect found.
gap_reasons: The exact shared-sign midpoint domination, double-occurrence reduction, and adjacent extremizer duplicate exp_delay_pairedwalk_exact_lattice_calibration and exp_delay_evenwalk_exact_calibration.
The proposed global survivor transport is the already-catalogued unresolved bottleneck of exp_delay_evenwalk_exact_calibration, not a new open problem.

proof_attempt_summary: Two non-identical proposal angles were attempted: assignment-law breadth and extremal discrete probability. The first failed credible nonduplicative seed breadth; the second duplicated two active paired-walk kernels and their calibration consequences, ending D-0.5 NO-PASS. No D0 derivation or Lean formalization occurred; no mathematical refutation was found, and the weighted frontier requires a separately presolved topic.
tldr: An independent fair assignment sign enters a cumulative experimental contrast at at most two fixed potential event times. The mathematical kernel is an extremal discrete probability statement: at every even barrier, every deterministic double-occurrence chronology has crossing probability at most that of adjacent duplicates, whose law is twice an ordinary simple-walk maximum. The proof target concerns the midpoint of two fixed permutations of the same signs, rather than exchangeable occurrence increments or a Gaussian approximation. An absorbing-walk evaluator then supplies a finite 95 percent calendar-time HT band with at most one count of excess radius under a specified integer constant-radius criterion. The aggregate survivor comparison is open; the proposal retains it as the indispensable all-size theorem.
gap: \cite{ChobanyanSalehi2001} and \cite{ChobanyanLeventalSalehi2015} provide convex or scaled maximal comparisons for zero-sum exchangeable systems. They do not determine the original-threshold crossing probability for a fixed relative permutation of the same independent signs. Gaussian tube comparisons also leave the discrete sign-cube count unresolved.
fill: Theorem 1 freezes the exact all-\(n\) even-barrier comparison. The open question exposes a global sign-cube transport handle. The evaluator, simultaneous causal coverage, and integer-radius guarantee are consequences, not independent seeds.
